basis: all188 literal output contracts reviewed before reference execution; no target-model output; fixed exclusion ids and reasons; no official train SPJ index assumed

rows.output_contract: Print two positive integers, $a$ and $b$, such that the value of $max(a, b)$ is minimum possible and $LCM(a, b)$ equals $X$. If there are several possible such pairs, you can print any.
For each of q queries output one integer number, the value that will appear in the corresponding array cell after Dima's algorithm finishes.

The first line should contain the minimum needed number of coatings n or -1 if it's impossible to create the desired coating.

If the answer is not -1, then the following n lines should contain two integers x_{i} and y_{i} — numbers of ending blocks in the corresponding piece. If x_{i} ≤ y_{i} then this piece is used in the regular order, and if x_{i} > y_{i} piece is used in the reversed order. Print the pieces in the order they should be glued to get the string t.
Print a string of Q characters, where the i-th character is '1' if the answer to the i-th query is positive, and '0' otherwise.
Print $t$ lines, the $i$-th of them should contain the maximum number of models that Orac can buy for the $i$-th query.
Print an only integer — the maximum possible value of the last slime.
In a single line print a single integer — the answer to the problem.

If there is a contradiction in the input and it is impossible to split the given sequence $a$ into one increasing sequence and one decreasing sequence, print "NO" in the first line.

Otherwise print "YES" in the first line. In the second line, print a sequence of $n$ integers $res_1, res_2, \dots, res_n$, where $res_i$ should be either $0$ or $1$ for each $i$ from $1$ to $n$. The $i$-th element of this sequence should be $0$ if the $i$-th element of $a$ belongs to the increasing sequence, and $1$ otherwise. Note that the empty sequence and the sequence consisting of one element can be considered as increasing or decreasing.
Print a single integer — the maximum number of pairs which can be made, adhering to the conditions in the statement.
Each of the t lines of the output should contain the answer to the corresponding input test set.

Print YES or NO in the first line depending on whether it is possible to make all elements equal in at most $n$ operations.

If it is possible, print an integer $m$ ($0 \leq m \leq n$), which denotes the number of operations you do.

In each of the next $m$ lines, print three distinct integers $i, j, k$, representing one operation. 

If there are many such operation sequences possible, print any. Note that you do not have to minimize the number of operations.
Output a single integer $t$ — the minimum time Bob needs to reach Alice.
Output a single integer — the number of good subarrays.

The first line of output must contain "YES" if there exist two arrays, such that the results of comparisons would be the same, and all numbers in the first one are distinct, and the second one contains two equal numbers. Otherwise it must contain "NO".

If the arrays exist, the second line must contain the array of distinct integers, the third line must contain the array, that contains at least one pair of equal elements. Elements of the arrays must be integers from $1$ to $n$.
Print single integer — maximum total damage creatures can deal.
Print a single word "YES", if the given sequence occurs in table G, otherwise print "NO".
Output the maximum possible length of a regular bracket sequence.
Print the maximum possible length of a subsegment of golden trophies, if Vova is allowed to do at most one swap.
Print $q$ lines. In the $i$-th line print one digit $x_i$ $(0 \le x_i \le 9)$ — the answer to the query $i$, i.e. $x_i$ should be equal to the element at the position $k_i$ of the sequence.

Output a single integer — the minimum time for which Denis can cross the road with obeying all the rules.

If it is impossible to cross the road output -1.

Print $n$ integers, the $i$-th number should be equal to the number of programmers, for which the $i$-th programmer can be a mentor. Programmers are numbered in the same order that their skills are given in the input.
Print the total number of times Vasily takes the top card from the deck.
For each test case print one integer — the minimum number of divisions required to fill the bag of size $n$ (or $-1$, if it is impossible).
Output the number of perfectly balanced striped binary search trees with $n$ vertices and distinct integer keys between $1$ and $n$, inclusive, modulo $998\,244\,353$.
For each test case, print the answer: the minimum number of moves you need to perform in order to make the sum of digits of $n$ be less than or equal to $s$.
Print a single integer — the number of suitable pairs.
Print the answer to each question on a single line. Print the answers in the order they go in the input.
Print one integer — the sum of weights of all partitions of a given set into k non-empty subsets, taken modulo 10^9 + 7.

For each query print one integer — the minimum number of characters you need to change in the initial string $s$ so that after changing there will be a substring of length $k$ in $s$ that is also a substring of the infinite string "RGBRGBRGB ...".
Print a single integer — the minimum number of actions needed to sort the railway cars.

On the single line print the single number — the answer.

Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit numbers in С++. It is recommended to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specificator.
Print one integer — the expected value of the number of crosswords Adilbek solves in $T$ seconds, expressed in the form of $P \cdot Q^{-1} \bmod (10^9 + 7)$.
For each test case output the minimal number of contests needed to infect all accounts.
Print two integers — the coordinates of the point that is not on the boundary of the square.
Print "YES" if it's possible to distribute all the pencils into boxes and satisfy all the conditions. Otherwise print "NO".

Print $n$ integer numbers — rearranged (reordered) input sequence that can be the sequence that Polycarp could write down on the board.

It is guaranteed that the answer exists.
Output a single line with N integers, where the i-th integer represents the total volume of snow melted on day i.
Output minimal width of the ad.
In the first line of the output print what Pasha's string s will look like after m days.

In the first line print $e$ — the number of edges that should remain in the graph ($0 \le e \le k$).

In the second line print $e$ distinct integers from $1$ to $m$ — the indices of edges that should remain in the graph. Edges are numbered in the same order they are given in the input. The number of good vertices should be as large as possible.
Print a single integer — the maximum number of frogs that can cross the river.
Print «YES» (without quotes) if it's possible to solve cube using one rotation and «NO» (without quotes) otherwise.
Print the k-th largest number in a n × m multiplication table.
Print two integers: the sum of Ciel's cards and the sum of Jiro's cards if they play optimally.

In a single line print a single integer — the maximum sum of query replies after the array elements are reordered.

Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
Print $n$ space separated integers $cnt_1, cnt_2, \dots, cnt_n$, where $cnt_i$ is equal to the number of points such that the number of segments that cover these points equals to $i$.

Write $q$ lines. The $i$-th of them should be YES if the religions could coexist in peace after the $i$-th evolution, or NO otherwise.

You can print each character in any case (either upper or lower).

For each test case, the first line of output should contain one integer $k$: the number of ways to divide $a$ into permutations $p_1$ and $p_2$.

Each of the next $k$ lines should contain two integers $l_1$ and $l_2$ ($1 \leq l_1, l_2 \leq n, l_1 + l_2 = n$), denoting, that it is possible to divide $a$ into two permutations of length $l_1$ and $l_2$ ($p_1$ is the first $l_1$ elements of $a$, and $p_2$ is the last $l_2$ elements of $a$). You can print solutions in any order.

If it is possible to rearrange the numbers in the date of birth so that Bob will be at least 18 years old on the DD.MM.YY, output YES. In the other case, output NO. 

Each number contains exactly two digits and stands for day, month or year in a date. Note that it is permitted to rearrange only numbers, not digits.
For each testcase print one line containing the largest beautiful number which is less than s (it is guaranteed that the answer exists).
For each test case, print one integer — the minimum number of operations Gildong has to perform in order to make all elements of the array equal.
If it is possible to connect Rebel spaceships and bases so as satisfy the constraint, output Yes, otherwise output No (without quote).
Print minimal number of seconds to eat at least $k$ candies. If solution doesn't exist, print "-1".
Print a single number — the minimum number of columns that you need to remove in order to make the table good.
Print a single integer — the remainder from division of Manao's minimum possible score in the quiz by 1000000009 (10^9 + 9).
Print one integer — the sum of values of the board over all $2^w$ possible ways to paint it, taken modulo $998\,244\,353$.
Print the maximum total friendship factir that can be reached.

On the first line output the number of values d for which Natasha can make the Martians happy.

In the second line, output all these values in increasing order.

Print all numbers in decimal notation.
Print one integer — the maximum possible number of occurrences of t in s as a subsequence if you replace no more than k characters in s optimally.

Print m integers: the j-th integer must show the number of spiders Om Nom will see if he starts his walk from the j-th cell of the first row. The cells in any row of the field are numbered from left to right.
Print a single integer number, the maximum number of letters that Nastya can remove.
Print a single integer — the answer to the problem modulo 1000000007 (10^9 + 7).
Print a single number: the minimum number of moves needed to get only numbers 1 in some column of the table. If this is impossible, print -1.

If there's no acceptable order of the people in the queue, print the single line containing "-1" without the quotes. Otherwise, print in n lines the people as "namei hi", where hi is the integer from 1 to 109 (inclusive), the possible height of a man whose name is namei. Print the people in the order in which they stand in the queue, starting from the head of the queue and moving to its tail. Numbers hi are not necessarily unique.
Output an integer: the maximal damage Jiro can get.
Print a single integer — the maximum number of points that Alex can earn.
For each bag print in separate line one single integer: the largest minimum distance between the eaten patty-cakes with the same filling amongst all possible orders of eating for that bag.
Print to the standard output t lines. The i-th line contains number of ants that Mole eats from the segment [li, ri].
Print a single integer — the number of seconds required to smash all the potatoes following the process described in the problem statement.
In a single line print an integer: the maximum number of coins the unlucky buyer could have paid with.

The first line should contain one integer number — the smallest number of nails needed to nail all the segments down. The second line should contain coordinates of driven nails separated by space in any order. If the answer is not unique, output any.
For each query print on a single line: either "Yes", if Alexey can enter the university, or "No" otherwise.

Print "NO" if no graph can be constructed under the given conditions.

Otherwise print "YES" and the diameter of the resulting graph in the first line.

The second line should contain a single integer $m$ — the number of edges in the resulting graph.

The $i$-th of the next $m$ lines should contain two integers $v_i, u_i$ ($1 \le v_i, u_i \le n$, $v_i \neq u_i$) — the description of the $i$-th edge. The graph should contain no multiple edges — for each pair $(x, y)$ you output, you should output no more pairs $(x, y)$ or $(y, x)$.

In a single line print $n$ integers, where the $i$-th number is:

  $-1$ if the line received after processing the first $i$ commands is not valid text,  the minimal number of colors in the case of the correct text.
Print the minimum number of seconds required to balance the load.
For each test case, print the answer on the separate line — the maximum possible sum of elements on even positions after reversing at most one subarray (continuous subsegment) of $a$.
Output a single integer — the value of min_{i} ≠ j  f(i, j).
Print a single integer — the number of possible pairs of words, such that their bitwise AND is equal to string s modulo 10^9 + 7.

Print a single integer — the number of distinct pairs of the tree's vertices which have a distance of exactly k between them.

Please do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
Print the remainder after dividing the required value by number mod.
Output a single integer, the maximum possible number of colors that the path can be painted in.
Output the minimal number of jumps that Jack requires to reach x.
Print a single string "Alice" if Alice wins; otherwise, print "Bob" (without double quotes).
Print a single number — the maximum length of the tandem repeat that could have occurred in the new string.
Print the maximal number of bouquets Fox Ciel can make.

Print $n$ integers $d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n$, where $d_i$ is the minimum the number of moves required to reach any position $j$ such that $a_j$ has the opposite parity from $a_i$ (i.e. if $a_i$ is odd then $a_j$ has to be even and vice versa) or -1 if it is impossible to reach such a position.
Output the number of the highest suitable branch. If there are none, print -1 instead.

The first line of the output should contain Yes if there exists a single non-zero area rectangular lair with corners on the grid for which checking the levels of Zombie Contamination gives the results given in the input, and No otherwise.
Print q lines, i-th line should contain a single integer — the answer to the i-th query.
In the single line print the result without spaces — the number after the k operations are fulfilled.
Print m lines. i-th of them must be equal to odd if the number of inversions in the permutation after i-th query is odd, and even otherwise.

For each test case, output one line containing YES if there exists an array a such that b_i is the median of a_1, a_2, ..., a_{2i-1} for all i, and NO otherwise. The case of letters in YES and NO do not matter (so yEs and No will also be accepted).
On the only line of the output print the size of the largest k-multiple free subset of {a_1, a_2, ..., a_{n}}.
Output the only integer — the number of interesting submissions.
Output n + 1 numbers — areas of the resulting parts in the increasing order.
Print a single integer — the maximum number of "nineteen"s that she can get in her string.
Output a single integer p, such that the smallest magical box that can contain all of Emuskald’s boxes has side length 2^{p}.
Print one integer — the answer to the problem, modulo 998244353.
Print "YES" (without the quotes), if string s contains two non-overlapping substrings "AB" and "BA", and "NO" otherwise.

Print the sequence of integers f1, f2, ..., fn, where fi (1 ≤ fi ≤ 2) is the number of a subject to which the i-th mark should be attributed. If there are several possible solutions, then print such that the sequence f1, f2, ..., fn is the smallest lexicographically.

The sequence p1, p2, ..., pn is lexicographically less than q1, q2, ..., qn if there exists such j (1 ≤ j ≤ n) that pi = qi for all 1 ≤ i < j, аnd pj < qj.

Print a single integer — the number of pairs of strings $r_0$ and $r_1$ that transform $s$ to $t$.

In case there are no such pairs, print $0$.
For the $i$-th query print the answer for it — "YES" (without quotes) if it is possible to turn some pipes in a way that the water flow can reach $(2, n + 1)$ from $(1, 0)$, and "NO" otherwise.
Print $n$ integers — the balances of all citizens after all events.
For each test case, print YES if you can obtain the sequence $b$ or NO otherwise. You may print each letter in any case (for example, YES, Yes, yes, yEs will all be recognized as positive answer).
If Richelimakieu can choose three musketeers, print the minimum possible sum of their recognitions. Otherwise, print "-1" (without the quotes).
Print a single integer — the maximum points Gerald can earn in this game.
In the first line print the maximum possible value of an expression.
For each test case, print the minimum number of seconds in which you can make $a$ nondecreasing.
Print "YES" if these fractions are equal and "NO" otherwise.
For each test case, output one number — the maximum number of gift sets that Polycarp can make.
Print the maximum possible length of the path segment in meters.

Print in the first output line "YES" (without the quotes), if the desired partition exists. In the second line output 4 space-separated numbers — point indexes from the input, which lie at the vertexes of the square. The points are numbered starting from 1. The numbers can be printed in any order. In the third line print the indexes of points lying at the vertexes of a rectangle in the similar format. All printed numbers should be pairwise distinct.

If the required partition does not exist, the first line should contain the word "NO" (without the quotes), after which no output is needed.
Print the only integer — the minimum possible length you can get after performing the operation described above any number of times.
Print $m$ lines. In the $j$-th line print the cost for the $j$-th customer.
Print a single integer — the minimal total amount of burles girls can spend to set the traps in order to guarantee that the mouse will eventually be caught no matter the room it started from.
Print two integers — the maximum number of blocks in the tower and the maximum required total volume X, resulting in the maximum number of blocks.

Print the number of possible ways how many people could be in the bus before the first bus stop, if the bus has a capacity equals to $w$. If the situation is contradictory (i.e. for any initial number of passengers there will be a contradiction), print 0.
Print one integer — minimum possible number of burles that mr. Funt has to pay as a tax.
Print t integers — the answers to the given test cases in the order they are written in the input.
For each query of type $2$ print "YES" if all the bills he has earned to this moment fit into a wallet of given size. Print "NO" otherwise.
Output the name of the winner: "Polycarp" or "Vasiliy".
Print the total number of subsequences "abc" in all strings you can obtain if you replace all question marks with letters "a", "b" and "c", modulo $10^{9} + 7$.
For each test case, print the minimum number of characters you need to erase from $s$ to make it good.

In the only line print $n$ integers. The $i$-th integer is equal to the number of blocks of length $i$.

Since these integers may be too large, print them modulo $998244353$.
Print one integer — the maximum possible value of defense plan reliability, i.e. the maximum possible value of minimum defense level if we distribute k additional archers optimally.
Print one number — minimal number of coins one friend can gift to satisfy all the conditions. If it is impossible to satisfy all three conditions print "-1" (without quotes).
Output one number for each question, separated by spaces — the number of different pitches.
Print the answer modulo $998244353$ in a single line.

Print "YES" (without quotes) if it is possible to transform $A$ to $B$ and "NO" (without quotes) otherwise.

You can print each letter in any case (upper or lower).
Output a single integer — the minimum number of plants to be replanted.
Print 2n integers — the permuted array a that minimizes the value of the sum s.
In a single line print a single integer — the answer to the problem.
For each query, print a single integer — the cost of the substring of the string $s$ from $l_i$-th to $r_i$-th position, inclusive.
Print the length of the longest possible Fibonacci-ish prefix of the given sequence after rearrangement.

For each question, print "YES" if Amugae can move from $(s_x, s_y)$ to $(e_x, e_y)$, and "NO" otherwise.

You can print each letter in any case (upper or lower).
Output the maximum value of a bitwise OR of sequence elements after performing operations.

On the first line print an integer $m'$ ($0 \leq m' \leq 3\cdot 10^5$), representing the number of debts after the consolidation. It can be shown that an answer always exists with this additional constraint.

After that print $m'$ lines, $i$-th of which contains three space separated integers $u_i, v_i, d_i$, meaning that the person $u_i$ owes the person $v_i$ exactly $d_i$ burles. The output must satisfy $1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$, $u_i \neq v_i$ and $0 < d_i \leq 10^{18}$.

For each pair $i \neq j$, it should hold that $u_i \neq u_j$ or $v_i \neq v_j$. In other words, each pair of people can be included at most once in the output.
For each query print one integer — the minimum number of magic crystals you have to spend to safely come down on the ground level (with height $0$).
Print the minimum number of moves required to collect all the treasures.

For each test case, output on a separate line:   YES, if it is possible to make all elements of the array equal to zero by applying a certain number of operations.  NO, otherwise. 

The letters in the words YES and NO can be outputed in any case.
In a single line print the remainder after dividing the answer to the problem by number 1000000007 (10^9 + 7).
Output one single integer — the minimum possible sum of the number of marks strictly below the water level among all days.
Print the number of possible values of $x$ that Qingshan can choose to make her win.

In case Petya can’t complete this level, output in the single line NO.

Otherwise, output on the first line YES. On the second line output the minimal time after which the boss can be defeated and the number of used scrolls. In the next lines for each used scroll output space-separated number of seconds passed from the start of the battle to the moment the scroll was used and the number of the scroll. Scrolls are numbered starting from 1 in the input order. The first scroll is considered to be available to be used after 0 seconds.

Output scrolls in the order they were used. It is not allowed to use scrolls after the boss is defeated.
Print one integer — the minimum number of operations to unify MST of the initial graph without changing the cost of MST.
For each test case, print the answer — the array $a$ of length $n$ after performing $n$ actions described in the problem statement. Note that the answer exists and unique.
For each abbreviation given in the input, find the year of the corresponding Olympiad.
Output two integers — the numerator and denominator of a fraction which is equal to the wanted average number. The fraction must be irreducible.
Print the minimum price of visiting the most extreme attraction for all pupils and their parents. Each of them should roll on the attraction exactly once.

In the first line print integer k (0 ≤ k ≤ n) — how many people can be leaders. In the next line, print k integers in the increasing order — the numbers of the people who can be leaders.

If the data is such that no member of the team can be a leader, print a single number 0.
Print one integer — smallest number of minutes to do all your laundry.
Print a single integer — the answer to the problem.

In the first line print the minimum number of coins that you need to spend to transform permutation p into permutation s.

In the second line print number k (0 ≤ k ≤ 2·10^6) — the number of operations needed to get the solution.

In the next k lines print the operations. Each line must contain two numbers i and j (1 ≤ i, j ≤ n, i ≠ j), which means that you need to swap p_{i} and p_{j}.

It is guaranteed that the solution exists.

Print the answer to the initial problem after each query — for the query $j$ print the maximum value of MEX after first $j$ queries. Note that queries are dependent (the array changes after each query) but operations are independent between queries.
For each test case, output the minimum number of days after which Polycarp will be able to buy a new computer.
For each view print the total brightness of the viewed stars.

If no configuration of targets exist, print $-1$.

 Otherwise, on the first line print a single integer $t$ $(0 \leq t \leq 2n)$: the number of targets in your configuration. 

 Then print $t$ lines with two spaced integers each per line. Each line should contain two integers $r$ and $c$ $(1 \leq r,c \leq n)$, where $r$ is the target's row and $c$ is the target's column. All targets should be different. 

 Every row and every column in your configuration should have at most two targets each.
Print the maximum possible value of the hedgehog's beauty.
For each test case, output the lexicographically maximum string that can be obtained after applying a certain sequence of operations after which all characters in the string become unique.
Print a single integer — the minimum number of beacons that could be destroyed if exactly one beacon is added.
Output the lexicographically smallest string that can be associated with some valid path after changing no more than $k$ letters in the matrix.

Print a single integer — the minimum number of preprocess moves to apply before changes, so that it is possible to make the string $a$ equal to string $b$ with a sequence of changes from the list above.
Output one integer — the reminder of division the answer by $1\,000\,000\,007$.
Print a single integer — the minimum number of moves needed to finish the game. If no sequence of turns leads to finishing the game, print -1.
Print a single integer — the number of ways to increase the sizes of the sticks by the total of at most l centimeters, so that you can make a non-degenerate triangle from it.
Print a single integer — the minimum total time needed to turn off all the lights.

In the first line of the output data print two numbers a and b (separate them by a space), where a is the maximum amount of books the organizers can include into the exposition, and b — the amount of the time periods, during which Berlbury published a books, and the height difference between the lowest and the highest among these books is not more than k milllimeters.

In each of the following b lines print two integer numbers separated by a space — indexes of the first and the last volumes from each of the required time periods of Berlbury's creative work.
Output a single integer — value of given expression modulo 10^{9} + 9.
Print one integer, which is the answer to the problem, modulo 998 244 353.
Print the total number of moves Alice and Bob will make.
In only line print one integer — the number of ways to divide the array $a$ modulo 998244353.
Print the number of unread notifications after each event.
Print one integer — the number of good substrings of string $s$.
Print the minimum time in seconds which Igor needs to get from the point x_1 to the point x_2.
Print a single integer, that means the minimum possible distance you need to cover to catch all the criminals.

For every request of the 1 type print number -1 on the single line if the corresponding car couldn't find place to park along the street. Otherwise, print a single number equal to the distance between the back of the car in its parked position and the beginning of the parking lot zone.
Print the minimum possible value of the sum described in the statement.
Print one integer: the maximum number of triples you can form.

In the first line print the minimum number of roads to be inversed if the capital is chosen optimally. In the second line print all possible ways to choose the capital — a sequence of indexes of cities in the increasing order.
In the only line print the number of subrectangles which form valid flags.
Print lexicographically minimal string that fits all the information Ivan remembers.
Print the maximum total beauty of exactly two fountains Arkady can build. If he can't build two fountains, print 0.

For each input set print the answer as a single line. Print a string of k letters "Y" or "N". Letter "Y" in position i should be printed if they could have run out of the i-th dish by the time the stewardess started serving Polycarp.
Print an only integer — the maximum score that can be achieved with the transformations. If it is not possible to perform even a single transformation for all possible starting integers, print $0$.

For each test case, print the answer — the minimum number of operations you have to perform to obtain at least one suitable path from the cell (1, 1) to the cell (n, m). It is guaranteed that the answer exists.
Print the only integer t — the minimum amount of time needed to generate the input file.
For each of the keys print one integer — the number of other keys that have the same fingerprint.
For each test case, output the maximum number of teleporters you can use.
